section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces the concept of error training, defining errors as deviations from goals that provide negative feedback necessary for learning. It describes a study by Frese et al. (1991) where an error training group was given minimal instructions and ample opportunities to make errors, while an error-avoidant group received detailed instructions. The error training group showed higher performance in tasks of medium and high difficulty, and the section argues that error training facilitates transfer performance by reducing the distance between training and transfer environments.
